competitors.title: Workflow SDK — Human-in-the-Loop

defineHook().create() must be called from workflow context, not from within a step

competitors.title: Workflow SDK — Hooks & Webhooks
key_points: createHook() is low-level primitive for pausing workflows and resuming with serializable data

competitors.title: Workflow SDK — Resumable Streams

startIndex parameter lets client choose where to resume — negative values supported

keywords: Vercel Chat SDK human in the loop
outline: Introduction: Why human-in-the-loop matters for production AI agents — the shift from stateless chatbots to durable, approval-gated workflows
Prerequisites: Node.js 18+, Chat SDK bot setup, Workflow SDK project configuration, Vercel account (for zero-config deployment)
Architecture Overview: How Chat SDK interactive cards + Workflow SDK createWebhook pair to eliminate approval databases, polling, and custom handlers
Step 1 — Setting Up the Workflow: Creating a durable workflow with 'use workflow' directive, installing Chat SDK and Workflow SDK packages
Step 2 — Defining the Approval Hook: Using defineHook() with Zod schema for type-safe approval data (approved boolean, optional comment)
Step 3 — Implementing the Approval Tool: Creating a tool that calls defineHook().create() with toolCallId as token, pausing at await hook
Step 4 — Creating the API Route: Building a POST endpoint that calls bookingApprovalHook.resume() to resume the workflow with approval data
Step 5 — Building the Approval Card Component: React component with Approve/Deny buttons, input display (flight number, passenger, price), optional comment textarea
Step 6 — Integrating with Chat SDK: Using callbackUrl on buttons to POST directly to the workflow's webhook URL, bypassing onAction handlers
Step 7 — Rendering Tool Status in Chat UI: Displaying tool-bookingApproval parts in the useChat message stream with the approval component
Alternative: createWebhook for Simpler Cases: Using createWebhook() directly when type-safe validation isn't needed — webhook URL can be emailed or logged
Multi-Stage Approvals: Chaining multiple createWebhook() calls with using scoping for sequential decision points within a single workflow
Timeout Safety: Racing createWebhook against durable sleep("24h") with Promise.race to prevent abandoned approvals from suspending forever
Stream Resumption with WorkflowChatTransport: Handling page refreshes, network interruptions, and serverless timeouts without losing agent progress
Cross-Platform Considerations: Platform-specific limits (Discord 100-char, Telegram 64-byte, Messenger/WhatsApp 20-char button titles) and workarounds
Security Best Practices: Token-based authentication for createWebhook vs createHook behind authenticated routes for sensitive operations
Troubleshooting: Stale button clicks, webhook URL mismatches, Discord/Telegram character limits, uncaught errors in workflow body
Conclusion: When to use Chat SDK alone (one-shot approvals) vs Chat SDK + Workflow SDK (durable multi-step processes with retries, timeouts, and observability)
